# I am excited to share that I have successfully completed my BEng degree in Civil Engineering with First Class Honours (1.1) at Heriot-Watt University. | Alastair Paterson · LinkedIn · 2025-11-30

**Alastair Paterson**: Based in United Kingdom [GB].

---

I am excited to share that I have successfully completed my BEng degree in Civil Engineering with First Class Honours (1.1) at Heriot-Watt University.

I was also presented with the Outstanding Graduate Apprentice Award, given in recognition of exceptional merit and performance in the during study undertaken as a graduate apprentice.

There have been many challenges along the way, studying and working alongside one another. However, over the four years the experience has been extremely rewarding and fulfilling, allowing me to apply theoretical knowledge to some of Scotland’s largest civil engineering projects.

I would like to thank [Farrans Construction](https://linkedin.com/company/farrans-construction) for facilitating my graduate apprenticeship and all those who have supported me throughout my studies over the 4 years.

Excited for what the future holds and the opportunities ahead!

That same year he also received a BSc Eng., with first class honours, from the University of Glasgow.

He had been in the OTC (Officer Training Corps) at school and university and, following assessment and selection, he was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the REME (Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers) which had only been established two years earlier, in 1942. Interview with Dr Alastair Paterson: Advice from an Old Hand – Agribook Digital

# Interview with Dr Alastair Paterson: Advice from an Old Hand

While you work, study as much as possible about your job so you become irreplaceable ... learn all the practicalities of your job.

Why agriculture? What drew your attention to agriculture?

I was born on a farm and enjoyed the arithmetic of agriculture especially finances.

How did you prepare for a career in agriculture? (training)

Left school at 16. Got a job on a farm.

I went to an agricultural college and five years later to University. Had a job on a huge farm in Johannesburg while studying and received Agric Honours, MSc and PhD.

Above: Alastair Paterson

When we first had contact you were working at Stockowners. People driving past on the N3 would have seen the building. What was Stockowners?

The company was actually developed in the 1930s to provide marketing services for Natal. I was offered a job here, was Head of the Production Division, supplying advice to 7,000 farmer members of Stockowners.

After Stockowners you spent years consulting on cattle production in the other countries to the north of here. What were the highlights of that time?
